title: US Seized a Ship with Crude Oil That Was Headed to Cuba and Sent It to Mexico
author: Jim Cason and David Brooks
content:
_This article by[Jim Cason and David
Brooks](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Jim%20Cason%20y%20David%20Brooks,%20corresponsales)
originally appeared in the [October 2, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/02/mundo/guardia-costera-
de-eu-intercepto-buque-con-combustible-hacia-cuba-nyt), Mexico's premier left
wing daily newspaper._

**Washington and New York**. The United States Coast Guard confirmed yesterday
that in early September it **intercepted, boarded and took control of a vessel
in international waters** , which, it alleges, was carrying oil to Cuba, and
afterward **escorted it to Puerto Progreso, Mexico** , where an inspection by
the Secretariat of the Navy (Semar) confirmed that the ship was loaded with
“large quantities” of fuel.

“Coast Guard interdicts Motor Vessel _Grace_ , continues operations to
interdict illicit fuel shipments to Cuba,” reads the headline of a press
release issued yesterday by the military branch. “In early September, a Coast
Guard tactical team boarded _Grace_ in the Caribbean Sea. _Grace_ was
transiting to Cuba, carrying fuel, and appeared to employ tactics common among
the _dark fleet_ ,” it added.

“The high seas are no sanctuary for illegality,” said Admiral Kevin Lunday,
commandant of the Coast Guard. “ _Dark fleet_ actors who employ deceptive
tactics to carry out illicit activities will not evade justice. The Coast
Guard is employing every capability to interdict these ships and enforce
international law.”

As of this edition's closing, Coast Guard spokespeople **had not responded to
specific questions from _La Jornada_ about what legal authority the US
government was using**, under national or global law, to intercept a ship in
international waters.

The press release adds that “after boarding, the Coast Guard escorted _Grace_
to Progreso, Mexico, where a Mexican Navy inspection team confirmed the
presence of large quantities of fuel in the vessel's ballast tanks.”

It reports that “the ship was also carrying several containers of what is
believed to be illicit fuel.”

The vessel tracking website VesselFinder, consulted by _La Jornada_ ,
identifies _Grace_ as a 100-meter-long container ship sailing under the flag
of the Comoros Islands, a country on the eastern coast of Africa. Another
search on the MagicPort website confirmed that the ship is currently in Puerto
Progreso and suggests that the owner is Arkon Capital Ltd, registered in Riga,
Latvia.

## Second Cargo Ship Detained This Year

Apparently, this type of capture was not the first. The Coast Guard press
release added that “the interdiction of _Grace_ came after the Coast Guard
boarded and detained the vessel _Jaira Provider_ , another vessel determined
to be carrying illicit fuel to Cuba earlier this summer.” It does not explain
what is illicit in the case of this hydrocarbon.

Although the title and first sentence of the press release assert that this
action was to enforce the US blockade against Cuba, further on it seems to
offer a different justification. “The unsafe storage of fuel in ballast tanks
poses an inherent danger to the marine environment. The actions of the United
States and Mexico prevented an unregulated transfer of fuel in the Caribbean
Sea, where deceptive shipping practices, unsafe vessel conditions and hidden
cargoes can increase the risk of oil spills and other pollution incidents that
threaten coastal communities, fisheries and sensitive marine ecosystems.”

The press release concluded by stating that “the United States Coast Guard
continued conducting operations to confront illicit maritime activity by
stateless _dark fleet_ vessels that fail to adhere to international norms.
These efforts are conducted consistent with international law as reflected in
the Law of the Sea Convention and in cooperation with flag and port state
authorities.”

In the end, it left no doubt that the goal of this operation was **to enforce
the blockade of Cuba**. “The Coast Guard concluded the successful interdiction
of … _Grace_ , following a coordinated international effort… confirming the
illicit trafficking of fuel to Cuba.”

That the release was issued almost a month after the capture, suggests
Professor Michael Bustamante, a specialist in Cuban-American studies at the
University of Miami, could have more to do with the midterm elections in the
United States than with anything else. That the Coast Guard “announces this
news a month later and a month before the midterms, I'll let you be the judges
of those timelines,” he wrote on his social media.

_La Jornada_ asked the Secretariat of Foreign Affairs (SRE) last night for
information on the participation of Mexican authorities in the operation, but
as of this edition's closing there was no response.
